title: Frank Trumbauer, horseback riding and bands at the Cinderella
summary: Moore and friends rode horses with Trumbauer in New Jersey; the Wolverines outlasted several bands at the Cinderella, with Fletcher Henderson nearby.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands

blocks.x: What do you, you say you knew Frank Trumbire fairly well?

We were real good friends. George Johnson and Frank and Bob and I, and Bob Gillette and I used to go over to East Orange, and about every Wednesday or Thursday, I forgot, in the afternoon, and go horseback riding. Frank always had an Indian pinto horse in his big hat. Of course he was on full-blooded Indian, you know, so you knew that I suppose. Who's this now? Frank Trumbire. And we used to have a great time going over there and going horseback riding over there. Dick didn't get in that part of it. He was resting up for the next night, the jam sessions. We used to go over here, Fletcher Henry's big Henderson's band all the time. Louis was with Fletcher Henderson that night.
In New York? When you were playing at the Cinderella? Yeah.
There was a band playing opposite you at the Cinderella, wasn't there?

Several. We outlasted three bands. Harold Oxley's band was one of them, and oh, the Dutchman Kruger, Willie Krieger, or something Krieger. These were all big bands. George Rapp used to be in there every night dancing. He was a terrific band. Charleston was born there at Cinderella when we were playing there.
